finding.claim: The /preview endpoint fetches any URL the caller supplies, with no validation. An attacker can make the server request internal services, cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254, or localhost. The first 500 characters of the response body and the status code are returned to the attacker, so this is full-read SSRF. Redirects are followed by default, which adds further reach.
finding.source: Query parameter `url` on GET /preview (request.args.get at app.py:15), supplied by any HTTP client
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16, with the response body returned at app.py:17

trace.note: target = request.args.get('url', '') takes the attacker-controlled value
requests.get(target) is called with no scheme, host, or IP check, and follows redirects
resp.text[:500] and the status code are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: There is no allowlist, no scheme restriction, no private-IP or DNS-resolution check, and no authentication on the route. The only control is the 5-second timeout, which does not prevent the request.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes the unauthenticated `url` query param and app.py:16 passes it straight to requests.get (redirects followed by default), returning the status and the first 500 body characters at app.py:17, with no host check. The ALLOWED_HOSTS check at app.py:24 exists only on the separate /partner route.
